newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa plans $500 mln Yankee bond issue - paper.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa plans $500 mln Yankee bond issue - paper.

text.p: South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel and his team plan to go to New York for roadshow next week to launch a 20-year Yankee bond issue of about $500 million, Business Day said on Monday.
The move, which has been widely expected, would likely complete the country's foreign borrowing target of four billion rand for 1997/98 (April-March).
The 2.5 billion rand from the dollar bond would enter the reserves in July, a month after the 1.5 billion rand from the 40 billion yen samurai launched last week, the paper said.

The two foreign issues will shore up reserves at a critical time for South Africa which is preparing to liberalise its foreign exchange controls on July 1 by allowing indidivuals to invest offshore for the first time.

The Reserve Bank is expected to consolidate foreign credit lines with the signing next month of a $1.5 million syndicated loan. Banking sources said the loan would be a flexible arrangement which the Bank would not draw on if it did not need to. U.S. investment bank Chase Manhattan has been tipped to lead the syndication.
